prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- To check whether AI chat/search engines recommend your business, use real-time, source‑citing generative search/chat engines: Perplexity.ai, Bing Chat (with sources), and Google’s Search Generative Experience (SGE). Also ask ChatGPT (with web access / browsing enabled).  
- For ongoing control so AIs are likely to recommend you, use a business knowledge/locator service such as Yext (plus standard local SEO tools like Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Yelp, BrightLocal).

Why those:
- Perplexity, Bing Chat, and Google SGE return answers with source links so you can see whether they cite or link to your site/listing. ChatGPT without browsing may be out of date or hallucinate, so use a version with browsing or the other engines for current checks.
- Yext (and similar knowledge-graph services) actively syndicates accurate business facts to many platforms and claims integrations with AI/search vendors — helping make you discoverable by these systems.

A simple plan you can follow
1. Claim and optimize your authoritative listings
   - Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Yelp, Apple Maps. Ensure name, address, phone, hours, website, categories, photos, and good reviews are present.
   - Add structured data (Schema.org LocalBusiness) on your website and ensure your site is crawlable.

2. Quick manual checks (what to use)
   - Perplexity.ai: search queries a potential customer would ask and see if it cites your site/listing.
   - Bing Chat (Edge or bing.com): ask conversational queries and inspect cited sources.
   - Google Search / SGE: enter the same queries and look for your listing or site in the answer/snippet.
   - ChatGPT with browsing (or GPT-4o with web access): ask the same prompts and request sources.

3. Example prompts to use
   - “I’m looking for [service] near [city/neighborhood]. Recommend 3 options and explain why.”  
   - “Best [service type] in [zip code / city]; include address, hours, and average rating.”  
   - “Where can I get [specific product/service] near me (address [your address])?”  
   - “Does [business name] in [city] provide [specific service]?”

4. Monitor and automate
   - For periodic automated checks use local-SEO monitoring tools: BrightLocal, Moz Local, Whitespark — they track local rankings, citations, and reviews.
   - For pushing canonical facts to many places use Yext (or a similar knowledge-graph provider).
   - If you want programmatic checks against LLMs, you can script queries to provider APIs (OpenAI, Bing Web Search API, etc.) and parse replies for mentions/links.

5. Improve chances of being recommended
   - Keep listings accurate and consistent (NAP).
   - Get strong reviews and respond to them.
   - Add structured data and FAQ/“What we do” pages on your site.
   - Earn links and mentions on local directories and reputable sites (AI answers favor authoritative sources).

Caveats
- Not all AI chat engines use the same sources or have up-to-date web access — results vary.
- Some LLMs may hallucinate; prioritize engines that provide source links.
- Being “recommended” depends on authoritative citations, user intent, and how your info is syndicated.

If you’d like, tell me your business name and city (or share a URL), and I’ll run a few sample queries across the major engines and report back what I find.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
